CLASS 29 · SIGHT WORDS

Learn the sight words, one card at a time.

Fifty-two sight word lessons, five minutes each: look at the card, say the word, play one tiny game and spot it in a real book. Start with a, the, I and you, then the action words, the colours and the little words that join sentences together.

Every lesson pairs with a printable card in the Sight Words flashcard set, and the lessons sit inside Class 29 · Storytime & Pre-Reading Comprehension on the Learning Path.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 52 cards in Sight Words, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Sight Words. We have 52 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · A

    “Read ‘a‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Spread five cards face up and ask your child to hand you the one that says a. Swap roles.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · The

    “Read ‘the‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Read a short rhyme aloud and tap the card each time you say the. Count the taps at the end.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · I

    “Read ‘I‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Take turns tapping your chest and finishing a sentence that begins with I.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · You

    “Read ‘you‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hold the card up to a teddy, to your child and to a family member, and say a sentence for each.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Me

    “Read ‘me‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hide the card, then peek it out from behind a book and say Look at me! Let your child do the same.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · My

    “Read ‘my‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Gather a few belongings on a rug and let your child claim each one aloud with my.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · We

    “Read ‘we‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Line up two or three stuffed animals with the card and say a we sentence about the whole group.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · It

    “Read ‘it‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Put a small toy under a cloth, lift it and say Here it is together.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Is

    “Read ‘is‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Take turns saying a true fact about the room that starts with the, such as The rug is soft.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Am

    “Read ‘am‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Whisper I am happy, then I am sleepy, then I am silly, and act out each one.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Are

    “Read ‘are‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Point at two toys and say Those are cars. Point at one and say That is a car.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Be

    “Read ‘be‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Draw a quick job on paper, hold up the card and say I want to be... Switch with your child.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Can

    “Read ‘can‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Have a challenge round: say I can and let your child prove it with a movement.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · And

    “Read ‘and‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Line up two pictures and say a short sentence joining them with and.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · In

    “Read ‘in‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hide a small toy in different containers and ask your child to say where it is: in the cup.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · To

    “Read ‘to‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Pass the card around a circle, saying I give it to...

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Up

    “Read ‘up‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Put a toy on a shelf and say Up, up, up! then take it down and say Down.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Down

    “Read ‘down‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Play up and down with a ball: say up as it goes up, down as it falls.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Go

    “Read ‘go‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hold up the card for green and tell your child to move, then hide it to stop.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Come

    “Read ‘come‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Use the card as a signal: hold it up and your child says Come! to someone.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Came

    “Read ‘came‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Ask What came in the mail? and let your child name something they saw come.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Run

    “Read ‘run‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Play run and freeze: run when you show the card, stop when you hide it.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Jump

    “Read ‘jump‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Make a pretend river with a rope and jump across it each time you say jump.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Play

    “Read ‘play‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Pick a toy, say I play with the toy, then take turns saying your own play sentence.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · See

    “Read ‘see‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Make binocular hands and say I see... for each thing you find in the room.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Look

    “Read ‘look‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Use a real magnifying glass to look at a leaf, a coin or the card itself.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Find

    “Read ‘find‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hide the card itself somewhere, say Find the card!, and let your child shout I find it.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Help

    “Read ‘help‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Role-play a pretend problem, such as a stuck jar, and practice asking for help.

  33. 30
    Card 29 · Make

    “Read ‘make‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Pick a tiny craft, such as a paper hat, and say each step with make.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Big

    “Read ‘big‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Use two toys of different sizes and say one is big and one is little.

  35. Cards 31–40
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Little

    “Read ‘little‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Pick two toys, say big and little, and swap them around.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Funny

    “Read ‘funny‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Take turns making funny faces and saying what is funny.

  38. 34
    Card 33 · One

    “Read ‘one‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hand your child one item at a time and say one each time.

  39. 35
    Card 34 · Two

    “Read ‘two‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Collect pairs of things and say two as you count them.

  40. 36
    Card 35 · Three

    “Read ‘three‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Put three apples or blocks on the table and say three together.

  41. 37
    Card 36 · Blue

    “Read ‘blue‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Grab a blue crayon and draw a blue picture while saying blue.

  42. 38
    Card 37 · Yellow

    “Read ‘yellow‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Draw a yellow sun and say yellow as you color it.

  43. 39
    Card 38 · Black

    “Read ‘black‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Draw a black night sky and say black as you color it.

  44. 40
    Card 39 · Brown

    “Read ‘brown‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Draw a brown tree trunk and say brown as you color it.

  45. 41
    Card 40 · Here

    “Read ‘here‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Play hide and seek and shout here when found.

  46. Cards 41–50
  47. 42
    Card 41 · Where

    “Read ‘where‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Hide the card somewhere in the room, ask Where is it? and let your child answer by finding it.

  48. 43
    Card 42 · Away

    “Read ‘away‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Put a toy away and say Put it away. Then bring it back out.

  49. 44
    Card 43 · At

    “Read ‘at‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Point at a place in the room and say I am at the window.

  50. 45
    Card 44 · By

    “Read ‘by‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Put a toy by the chair, then by the door, and say by each time.

  51. 46
    Card 45 · For

    “Read ‘for‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Wrap a toy in paper and say This is for you.

  52. 47
    Card 46 · Not

    “Read ‘not‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Say yes and not sentences about objects and let your child say the other.

  53. 48
    Card 47 · But

    “Read ‘but‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Say a sentence with but and let your child finish it.

  54. 49
    Card 48 · All

    “Read ‘all‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Count everyone in the family and say all of us.

  55. 50
    Card 49 · Said

    “Read ‘said‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Retell a short conversation from your day using said, and let your child do the same for you.

  56. 51
    Card 50 · Ate

    “Read ‘ate‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Draw what you ate and write ate next to it.

  57. Cards 51–52
  58. 52
    Card 51 · Did

    “Read ‘did‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Pick a small job, such as tidying a toy, do it together and let your child say I did it!

  59. 53
    Card 52 · Could

    “Read ‘could‘ aloud, then find it again in a favorite book.”

    How: Brainstorm three ideas with could at the start.

  60. 54
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  61. 55
    Check

    “Can you find A? Now show me Find.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  62. 56
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 52 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
